newsitem.title: USA: US House tax chief--kill ethanol subsidy by 2000.
newsitem.headline: US House tax chief--kill ethanol subsidy by 2000.

text.p: The chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee underlined his intention to end ethanol subsidies in 2000 and said he would not allow an extension to become law.

"I believe that the extension that is in the Senate bill that came out of committee, if it survives the floor, will be removed in the (House-Senate) conference committee," chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, told reporters. A House-Senate conference committee will write a final version of the bill.

Archer said the tax bill written by the Ways and Means Committee would send "a clear message to the ethanol community there will be no extension beyond the year 2000, so they should not build new facilities...in expectation Congress might extend the subsidy."

His committee's bill would slightly reduce the ethanol subsidy -- reducing it by 0.1 cent to 5.3 cents per gallon at the fuel pump -- and eliminate the fuel tax break in 2000, as now scheduled in law.
The Senate bill would extend the fuel tax break until 2007 but gradually lower it to 5.1 cents a gallon.

Ethanol proponents have hoped to out-flank Archer, a longtime foe, by preserving the tax break in the Senate. They also have been cheered by statements of support for ethanol by leaders like House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Georgia Republican.
Archer lumped ethanol among the group of costly and unneeded alternative fuels given tax breaks during the embargo-fearing 1970s.

There might be some change in terminology in the ethanol language as the tax bill as it was prepared for debate later this week in the House, Archer said, but it would be aimed at ensuring an end to the tax break.
